summary: Error-bar half-widths of every series in Katsounaros thesis Diag 12.3 (the thesis copy of Katsounaros et al. 2012 Fig. 1). Every bar that can be measured is +-10.0% of the plotted value: 18 well-resolved bars (half-width >= 5 px) give 0.0997 +- 0.0010 (range 0.0968-0.1013), 8 small bars give 0.103 +- 0.010, all within their reading error of 0.100. The bars are a constant relative percentage (the plotting program's percent-of-data style), not per-point replicate statistics. The thesis does not describe them.

calibration.note: Tick marks located on the image by darkness profiles beside the axis lines (ticks point outward); all 11 y ticks (majors every 100 mM, 15 px long; minors at the 50s, 8 px) fitted by least squares. Agrees with the xcheck calibration (0.59793 mM/px) to 0.03%.

method: Each bar is a 1 px vertical line with a 1 px horizontal cap about 17 px wide at each end (measured on 14 clean caps: darkness integral 0.96, anti-aliased at quarter-pixel positions). Bars are drawn over the markers, and the bar line runs from the marker edge to the cap, so caps inside open (white-filled) markers stay visible; caps inside filled markers do not. Every cluster was inspected in pixel dumps and zoomed crops. Each visible cap was then located by the darkness-weighted centroid of the median-over-columns profile in a small row window, with columns chosen to avoid marker outlines, model curves and other series' caps (per-cap windows and columns in the script). One cap (NO3 at 90 min) is split over two rows of which only one is clean; its row is that row + (1 - darkness/0.96). Centre = cap midpoint when both caps are visible, else the xcheck marker centre. half_width = |cap - centre|; relative = half_width / centre. half_width_sd from the cap position uncertainty (0.15 px clean, 0.2-0.5 px occluded; +0.5 px for the centre when only one cap is visible). Overlay of all caps on the page checked by eye (scratch, not committed).

thesis_text_on_error_bars: Neither the caption nor the text of Diag 12.3 (printed pp. 191-192) mentions the bars, and no passage in the thesis describes error bars. Related statements: printed p. 81, the deviation of the selectivity sum from 100% 'is due to the experimental error, which was of the order of 10%' (a -2.4 V NaCl run); printed p. 146, mass-balance loss within the experimental error (+-5%) for nitrate below 0.1 M; printed p. 71, ion chromatography of hyponitrite/hyponitrate RSD 5% (9 repeats); printed p. 192, model fit '% error = 9.3%', defined in the appendix (printed p. 201) as sum|residual| / sum(measured). The +-10% bars match the 'order of 10%' experimental error. They are a uniform percentage, not per-point replicate statistics, and their type (1 sigma, 2 sigma, range) is not stated.
use_as_noise_model: If adopted, take relative_sigma = 0.10 for all five species (NO3, NO2, N2, NH3, N2O in mM-N) in the task noise model (schema/task.schema.json noise.relative_sigma), or sigma_i = 0.10 x y_i per point (dataset.schema.json series sigma). Add an absolute floor (absolute_sigma_mM) for near-zero points, since a pure relative sigma is zero at t = 0 and below 0.5 mM for NH3 and N2O at 30 min. This is an author-assigned uniform error of unstated type, not measured scatter: if the bars are 2 sigma or a max-error range, the 1-sigma value would be about 0.05.

byproducts.cap_midpoint_centres: Where both caps are visible the cap midpoint is an independent estimate of the plotted value. It agrees with the xcheck marker centres to <= 0.5 px (0.3 mM) except NO3 at 60 min (123.5 mM from caps vs 122.0 from the occluded template match; the square's bottom edge gives 123.6; Daniel 123.9), NH3 at 120 min (25.8 vs 26.2) and NH3 at 150 min (23.8 vs 24.3). NH3 at 120 min from the caps (25.8 mM) supports the thesis marker over Daniel's 19.6 for the thesis copy only (the journal figure Daniel digitized was not checked); see the integration note in ../katsounaros2009thesis_diag12p1_intermediates (the Diag 12.1 NH3 rates imply about 20.8).
